blocks.text: To the dreamland that every traveller carries within them.

On the very edge of historic Tibet, there once existed a small kingdom whose landscapes resembled the dawn of the world, harbouring a sacred Tibetan heritage that has endured through the centuries and where spirits still dwell… Between past and present, dream and reality, Myths and beliefs, Shangri-La and Shambala, An exploration proposed, an invitation to meditate, On this secret land that each of us carries within. Then to dare, to dream.

Through analogue photographs and poetic prose, Shambala reveals itself. Shambala, that mythical realm, a place of wisdom and peace accessible through spiritual purity by attaining Enlightenment, lies within each of us. This artistic journey presents itself as a unique testimony that weaves together the threads of past, present and future, dream and reality, myths and beliefs, to recreate, in its own way, the soul of a land with exceptional natural and cultural heritage. The timeless monochrome here reinforces the quest for Shambala, creating a space-time where impermanence reigns supreme. Fine art prints reveal the texture of the images; photographic diptychs resonate with one another; large-format works emphasise the majesty of the landscapes: from this alchemy emerges a fluid, ethereal and sensitive photographic journey. Poetic captions outline the contours of a rapidly changing region, introduce the spiritual dimension of an authentic Tibetan culture, and reveal absolute beauty.

A work that draws its inspiration from the account *Mustang, the Forbidden Tibetan Kingdom* by Michel Peissel, a French writer and ethnologist who was the first Westerner to be granted permission to visit Mustang in 1964 – a region then closed to foreigners – and who showed us the way to our dream. (Texts by Marjolaine Edouard)
